correctness.rationale: The order ideal/column-bit representation is bijective for each n>=2. The successor is derived directly from the minimal complement and yields an exact finite-state support projection. All 48 possible nonempty support configurations are classified into 13 explicit cycles, with correctly computed symbol permutation orders; a surjective word uses every symbol, forcing exact period p*q. Orbit formulas follow by onto-word inclusion-exclusion. A standalone package verifier recomputes the support orbits and tests an independently implemented direct ideal/toggle map for n=2..6; finite enumerations are checks, not the uniform proof. Boundary n=2 is included and has no 6/24 cycles; n>=3 has 24 cycles.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-n enumeration, not a small empirical increment: arbitrarily large incidence posets with exponentially many ideals have uniformly bounded rowmotion order exactly 24. The six explicit orbit formulas, period spectrum and primitive-cycle threshold expose the dynamical mechanism via just 48 support states. Such parameter-wide orbit structure is a natural and reusable invariant in algebraic combinatorics. The result does not claim a new general birational period theorem.
